# FP07 in-situ calibration sheet

**23 calibrations of 12 FP07 beads**, 2019-06-02 to 2025-04-10.

This page is generated from [`fp07_calibrations.yaml`](fp07_calibrations.yaml), the single source of truth. [`fp07_calibrations.csv`](fp07_calibrations.csv) is the same entries, one row per fit, for spreadsheets. Never edit either view by hand: edit the YAML, then run `fp07-cal registry render`. `fp07-cal registry check` (and the test suite) fails when a view is out of date.

## How to read this sheet

**An entry** is one FP07 bead (by its Rockland serial, e.g. T1592) in one deployment, calibrated in situ by `fp07-cal fit` against a reference thermometer on the same vehicle. All of a deployment's profiles are pooled into one fit. Beads move between channels and instruments, so a bead's history can span several instruments.

**The equation.** The coefficients are in the form a Rockland `.p` configuration carries, which ODAS and this package (`rsi/channels.py::convert_therm`) read and `fp07-cal patch` writes:

```
1/T_K = 1/t_0 + L/beta_1 + L^2/beta_2 + L^3/beta_3        T [degC] = T_K - 273.15
```

`t_0` and every `beta` are in kelvin, and each `beta` is a *reciprocal*. A fit of order n has `beta_1` .. `beta_n`, and an absent term is no term. To switch a term off in a `.p` config that carries it, write `beta_2 = 1e30`, never `0` (zero would be an infinite term). `t_0` and `beta_1` trade off strongly against each other, so do not compare entries by `t_0` alone; compare the temperatures they imply at the same L.

**What L is.** `L = ln(R_T/R_0)`, the log of the bead's resistance relative to the bridge's reference resistor. It is computed from raw counts through the channel's half-bridge constants:

```
Z = ((counts - a)/b) * (adc_fs / 2^adc_bits) * 2 / (g * e_b)      L = ln((1 - Z)/(1 + Z))
```

Z is clipped to ±0.6 (as ODAS does), so L never leaves ±ln(1.6/0.4) = ±1.386; a sample on the clip is out of the bridge's range, not a temperature. Each entry records the six constants (`a`, `b`, `g`, `e_b`, `adc_fs`, `adc_bits`) because the coefficients describe T as a function of *this* L. Copied to a channel with different constants (another instrument, or the other channel of the same one), the same coefficients give a different temperature.

**How to use an entry.** Copy `t_0` and the `beta` terms into the channel's section of the `.p` configuration, provided its bridge constants are the ones listed. **Remove any legacy `beta` key from that section**: ODAS and `convert_therm` read `beta` before `beta_1`, so a pasted `beta_1` is silently ignored while `beta` is there. Then run perturb with `fp07.calibrate: false`. Full precision is in the YAML and the CSV; the tables here are rounded to well below 0.1 mK. Use an entry only inside its fitted temperature range, since a polynomial is not constrained outside it. Where the deployment has its own reference, its own pooled fit (`fp07-cal fit`, see `docs/fp07cal/runbook.md`) is better than any entry here. An entry's prior is for when a full fit is impossible, and the history is for QC.

**What the uncertainties mean.** Each is a temperature error in mK, measured against that entry's reference:

- *rms*: root-mean-square residual of the fit against the reference, in sample, over the pairs its robust 4-sigma clip kept. For fits made with `fit.prior` the notes also give the rms over every pair (`rms_all_mK`): a shape that does not fit clips the ends of the range and looks better over the pairs it kept.
- *held-out*: rms error predicting the cold half of the range from a fit to the warm half, and vice versa. It measures how well the shape extrapolates, and it chose the order where the order is `auto`. Where the order is `prior`, the shape was held fixed from the bead's calibration named in the notes and only `t_0` was fitted (`fp07-cal fit` with `fit.prior`); held-out is then that fit's.
- *block SD*: the deployment is cut into equal-time blocks, each block's `t_0` offset is refitted with the shape held fixed (fp07-cal's stability check), and this is the standard deviation of those offsets. It measures how far the calibration wandered within the deployment. It is left blank below 3 blocks.

None of them includes the reference's own error. The *cal. age* column is how long the reference had gone without a calibration when the deployment began.

The same limit applies between deployments. Every SN194 comparison was made through the same reference, JAC CT SN 23 (calibrated 2016-02-15), so a change in a bead cannot be separated from drift of that reference. Against a fresher JAC (SN 79, calibrated 2021-10-20) on ARCTERX-2022 Interior, mixed-layer casts within 30 minutes of each other give JAC 23 - JAC 79 = +15 mK (n = 29, MAD 19 mK). That is suggestive only: the two VMPs alternated rather than profiling together, so it is confounded with position and time (+13 mK when SN194 cast second, +30 mK when it cast first). A recalibration of JAC 23 would settle it.

### Prior for a fresh deployment

Each bead's section ends with a prior: a starting calibration for a deployment where a full in-situ fit is impossible (too little reference, or too narrow a temperature range to constrain the shape). The rule:

> The coefficients, shape and t_0 alike, come from the bead's widest-range unflagged calibration: the widest fitted temperature range among calibrations not flagged `short`, `fast-descent` or `episode` (ties go to the more recent), counting only calibrations that ended by `as_of` when one is given. A calibration whose shape was itself held fixed from a prior (order `prior`) never supplies one: its shape was not fitted over its range. With a target instrument (serial; 'SN' and leading zeros are ignored) and optionally a channel (any case), the widest unflagged calibration on that instrument and channel is preferred. If there is none, the bead's widest unflagged calibration is used, and the cross-instrument term is added to t_0 in quadrature. If the bead has no unflagged calibration, its widest-range calibration is used (on the target when possible); the prior says so and adds that fit's held-out error to the shape term in quadrature. t_0 carries the sheet's carried-over offset uncertainty, and the shape the sheet's shape uncertainty. The prior reports the union of the bead's fitted ranges (outside the source's own range the shape is extrapolated) and how far the most recent calibration is from it, at the center of their common fitted range.

The transfer uncertainties come from comparing the same beads across deployments and years ([issue #189](https://github.com/mousebrains/turbulence/issues/189#issuecomment-6475966024)). They are typical observed magnitudes from a handful of beads, not bounds and not formal standard errors; the evidence column gives the largest seen:

| term | typical size | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| t_0 carried over to a new deployment | ±15 mK | From the entries in this sheet, two curves of one bead compared at the same L (registry.curve_difference). T1592 on VMP SN194 at 28 degC, against ARCTERX-2022 Interior: -11.6 mK (SUNRISE 2019), -2.9 and -3.6 mK (SUNRISE 2021), -9.2 mK (SUNRISE 2022), +0.2 mK (ARCTERX-2022 Wake). T1593 from 2019 to 2021: +9.5 to +17.1 mK over 26.56-29.40 degC, the largest seen. T2005 within -0.5 to +3.4 mK of ARCTERX-2022 Interior over four deployments in 2021-2022. MicroRider SN435's beads T2811 and T2813 one year apart (2025 to 2026; #189 analysis, not in this sheet): -10.6 and -13.2 mK. The #189 comment quotes order-2 fits, which differ from these auto-order entries by up to ~3 mK (SUNRISE 2019: -14 mK there). All the VMP numbers were seen through one JAC CT (see the reference caveat). |
| curve shape (`beta` terms) | ±5 mK over 5-10 K | Quiet-water fits only. Over the common range of two calibrations of one bead the curves differ by 1.2-3.8 mK peak-to-peak (T1592 and T2005 against ARCTERX-2022 Interior, including T1592 on another instrument in 2025: 2.5 mK over 5.4 K); T2811 and T2813 one year apart (#189, not in this sheet) by 2.9 and 4.0 mK over 5-18.6 degC. Fast descents break this: T1592's SUNRISE 2019 and 2022 curves differ from ARCTERX-2022 Interior by 16.1 and 16.7 mK peak-to-peak, which is why `fast-descent` disqualifies a prior source. |
| other instrument or channel | 10 mK, added to t_0 in quadrature; one observation | One observation. T1592, moved from VMP SN194 T1 (2022) to VMP SN142 T2 (2025), reads -8.3 to -10.8 mK (mean -9.1) against its ARCTERX-2022 Interior curve at the same L over 19.85-25.26 degC; the #189 fixed-curve comparison against each JAC gives +9.8 mK, the same shift seen from the bead's side. It combines bead change, other bridge electronics and another JAC CT (SN 22). |
| settling in a new deployment | 5-10 mK over the first 7-14 days | Long Slocum and MicroRider deployments (ARCTERX-2023 and 2025 Interior, #189): a common settling of 5-10 mK over the first 1-2 weeks, besides episodes of 10-40 mK tied to electrical faults. |

A `t_0`-only refit (the shape held fixed from the prior) removes the first term and needs almost no temperature range. `fp07-cal fit` does it when its config has a `fit.prior` block. It keeps that refit unless the full fit is clearly better on held-out error, and always over a range narrower than the shape span or when no full fit is a plausible curve for the bead. It flags a result outside the prior's uncertainty over their common range: a possible unrecorded bead swap, reference problem or failing bead (see `docs/fp07cal/runbook.md`). `fp07-cal registry show <serial>` prints a bead's prior, with `--instrument`/`--channel` for a different target and `--as-of` to use only calibrations that had ended by a date. `fp07-cal registry add` records a fit here from its `coefficients.json`.

### Flags

| flag | meaning |
|---|---|
| `lag-gate-overridden` | fp07-cal's lag-trust gate, tuned for gliders, rejected the lag. It rejects every VMP lag (issue #238), so the fit was kept. `fp07-cal patch` would refuse the original record; use the coefficients here directly. |
| `export-gate-overridden` | fp07-cal's 1 K export gate refused the first fit, and the deployment was refitted with the gate raised. The notes say why. |
| `reference-edited` | Reference samples were blanked beyond fp07-cal's own QC. The notes say which and why. |
| `screened` | Part of the deployment was left out of the fit. The dates are those of the data actually used. |
| `episode` | The fitted data contain an offset episode, typically an electrical fault. It inflates the scatter; the notes say when and how large. |
| `short` | Too little data (files, profiles or days) for the block scatter, or a drift, to mean much. |
| `fast-descent` | Fast VMP descents through strong gradients, where the reference's own response biases the pooled curve. The block scatter is several times the quiet-water figure. |

### Methods

| method | how the fits were made |
|---|---|
| `glider-ctd` | fp07-cal fit against the Slocum's own CTD (sci_water_temp on sci_ctd41cp_timestamp), real samples only, pooled over up to 100-160 files spread across the deployment. A 0.7 s single pole for the CTD's thermistor; lag searched over +/-20 s after a 30 s high-pass and gated on peak sharpness; robust fit with the sensor-geometry term (dz*dT/dz + tau*w*dT/dz) fitted jointly. In every glider fit here dz and tau are collinear (0.86-0.94), so only their combination is resolved. |
| `vmp-own-jac` | fp07-cal's run_calibration (the engine of `fp07-cal fit`) pooled over every VMP descent of the deployment (P >= 3 dbar, fall rate >= 0.3 dbar/s, >= 20 s) against the instrument's own JAC CT temperature (JAC_T): every 8th slow sample, none interpolated, blanked over bad buffers plus 2 s, and +/-3 s around any sample more than 1 K from its 0.5 s running median (this fired once, on SN142 in ARCTERX-2025 Interior). The reference pole is a single pole at the JAC's vendor response for the median fall rate. Lag searched over +/-1 s after a 10 s high-pass; robust fit; the sensor-geometry term off, because the 2021 descents span about 22 dbar, too short for it. |

### FP07 time constant (`response`)

An entry may carry the bead's FP07 time constant, measured by `fp07-pair tau` from the deployment's chi products and recorded with `fp07-cal registry response` (`docs/fp07pair/runbook.md`). It is a property of the bead, carried with the bead's calibration (the PI's decision, 2026-10-28).

**What the number is.** Each bead's single-pole-equivalent time constant over 1-25 Hz: a single pole, |H|^2 = 1/(1 + (2 pi f tau)^2), fitted to each bead of a pair from the ratio of their gradient spectra, at the pair's median speed `W_ref`. Two beads on one probe head see the same microstructure, so the ratio needs no turbulence model. **The pole form is not determined**: a double pole fits the ratio as well and puts the 3-dB point 30-40% lower. **The absolute level is family- and band-dependent** (on ARCTERX-2022 SN194 the same products give 17/25 ms fitted over 1-25 Hz and 11/17 ms over 1-60 Hz, and spectral sums over 1-26 Hz gave 13/20) **and no external reference anchors it**: the in-situ anchor failed its synthetic check (`docs/fp07_tau_prefactor_PLAN.md`). The electronics contribute negligibly: the anti-alias filters sit near 110 Hz, far above the band, so this is the bead's tau. **The ratio is the robust part**, recorded model-free as this bead's power response over its partner's at 10 and 20 Hz, relative to the reference band (the lowest well-sampled bins below 4 Hz). The time halves show a bead that changed within a deployment.

**Identified or not.** Matched beads give a flat ratio and no tau, and a failing bead (one that loses amplitude, or goes dead) has no time constant to measure. A pair is identified only when the beads differ beyond bootstrap noise at 20 Hz, each tau's 16-84% interval is bounded and spans at most a factor 1.5, the flat gain is below a factor 2, neither bead is dead in any chi file of the span, and there are enough chi files, recordings and frequency points (the full rule is in the runbook). The intervals come from resampling whole recordings (`.p` files), and they are sampling intervals only: the choice of estimator and band moves the level by more. Otherwise tau is blank and only the power ratios are recorded.

**At 1 m/s** the table shows tau scaled from `W_ref` under the entry's `speed_scaling` (`lueck`: tau ~ W^-1/2). That column is derived, never stored. For comparison, the `lueck` default chi uses is 10 ms at 1 m/s; across the fleet beads scatter by a factor ~1.9 (geometric 1 sd) about a median of ~12 ms, which is why tau is carried per bead. Nothing in chi processing reads these values yet.

| method | what it does |
|---|---|
| `pair-ratio-sp` | `fp07-pair tau`: one single pole per bead fitted to the median over windows of ln(S2/S1), the bead pair's gradient-spectrum ratio from the deployment's chi products (built as `fp07-pair fit` builds it), read every 1 Hz across `band_Hz` of reduced frequency (frequency at the pair's median speed `W_ref_m_s`, windows at other speeds mapped by `speed_scaling`), with 16-84% intervals from a bootstrap over chi files. The flat gain between the beads is a free parameter. |

| response flag | meaning |
|---|---|
| `amplitude` | Flat gain between the beads beyond a factor 2: an amplitude-loss signature (a failing bead). Never a tau measurement. |
| `dead-bead` | One bead's gradient spectrum was identically zero (a dead or railed channel) through whole chi files of the span: a failing bead. Those files were left out, and the pair is never a tau measurement; `reason` names the bead and the files. |
| `outlier` | The 20 Hz power ratio is beyond the fleet spread (\|ln\| > 0.9): possibly a failing bead, or one far slower than its partner. |
| `noise-model` | In its quietest windows one bead's observed spectrum at 60-100 Hz is more than 1.5x off its noise model, which biases tau. |
| `drift` | This bead's two time halves differ by more than twice their combined 1-sigma (16-84%) uncertainty: it changed within the deployment (fouling, aging). |
| `ratio-shift` | The pair's 20 Hz power ratio differs between the time halves by more than twice their combined 1-sigma: this bead, its partner, or both changed within the deployment. Model-free, so more sensitive than `drift`, but it cannot say which bead (compare the halves' taus). |

Notes:

1. **SUNRISE 2019 Pelican**: Median fall rate 1.28 dbar/s through strong gradients. The six block offsets span 10.4 mK, against 1-3 mK on the quieter deployments.
2. **SUNRISE 2021 Pelican**: All 16 Pelican files. T2 was changed from T1593 to T2005 on 2021-06-29; T1 fits split at that change agree with this one to 0.1 mK at 27-28 degC. The range is only 2.8 K, so the shape is weakly constrained. FP07 time constant: Measured against T2005, which replaced T1593 on T2 on 2021-06-29 (the last 5 recordings); against T1593 the pair is refused (T1593 dead in SR1P_516, see its entry). From the swap on, both probes' observed high-frequency floor is 0.2-0.5x their noise model, against ~1 before it (noise-model).
3. **SUNRISE 2021 WaltonSmith**: The range is only 1.9 K, so the shape is weakly constrained. FP07 time constant: Both probes' observed high-frequency floor is 0.3-0.4x their noise model (noise-model), as on the Pelican after the T2 swap.
4. **ARCTERX-2022 Interior**: The baseline for the cross-deployment comparisons in issue #189. FP07 time constant: The acceptance case: on the same chi_00 products the analysis-era first pass (spectral sums) gave 13.0/19.5 ms and its median-of-log fit 17.4/25.6 (docs/fp07pair/runbook.md section 6).
5. **ARCTERX-2022 Wake**: Only 2 files (36 descents) carried this bead. 2 blocks, so no block scatter. FP07 time constant not identified: 1 recordings (distinct start times) < 5; no bootstrap interval for the 20 Hz ratio; 0 of 200 bootstrap replicates fitted; tau1: no interval; tau2: no interval. FP07 time constant: ARC1A044 only: the products of ARC1A046.P were made before the mis-framing fix (bdd0a4d) and are left out. One recording, so no interval and no tau.
6. **SUNRISE 2022 PointSur**: fp07-cal's 1 K export gate refused both channels over one 4 K event at a bottom-layer front, which the robust fit had already discarded. Refitted with the gate at 10 K and a +/-0.5 s lag search. Median fall rate 0.96 dbar/s through strong gradients; the six block offsets span 9.8 mK. FP07 time constant: T2's quiet-window floor is 1.5x its noise model at 60-100 Hz and up to 23x at 150-250 Hz, T1's about 1: excess high-frequency content on T2, which makes T2005 look fast. Treat T2005's value here as suspect (see its entry).
7. **ARCTERX-2025 Interior**: Moved to VMP SN142, channel T2, so other bridge constants and another JAC CT. 3 of SN142's 5 files had descents. The reference was blanked +/-3 s around one instrument-wide transient (AIOP2_VMP142_0002 at 21:14:22Z: JAC_T to 5 degC and P +3 dbar within 0.1 s, both FP07s ramping together). At the same L this curve reads -8.3 to -10.8 mK (mean -9.1) against the bead's ARCTERX-2022 Interior curve over 19.85-25.26 degC, a nearly flat shift. FP07 time constant not identified: 3 recordings (distinct start times) < 5. FP07 time constant: Only 3 recordings (chi_01 products).

### Prior for a fresh deployment of T1592

From **ARCTERX-2022 Interior** (vmp-250 SN 194 T1, 2022-03-21 to 2022-03-30), the widest-range unflagged calibration. Order 3.

| t_0 [K] | beta_1 [K] | beta_2 [K] | beta_3 [K] |

2. **SUNRISE 2021 WaltonSmith**: The range is only 1.9 K. Order 2 beat order 1 by 0.09 mK of held-out error and gives a negative beta_2, so do not extrapolate this shape. FP07 time constant: Noise model 2-3x above the observed floor on both probes (noise-model).

FP07 time constant not identified: 1 recordings (distinct start times) < 5; no bootstrap interval for the 20 Hz ratio; 0 of 200 bootstrap replicates fitted; tau1: no interval; tau2: no interval. FP07 time constant: ARC1A044 only (ARC1A046.P's products predate the mis-framing fix).
5. **SUNRISE 2022 PointSur**: fp07-cal's 1 K export gate refused both channels over one 4 K event at a bottom-layer front, which the robust fit had already discarded. Refitted with the gate at 10 K and a +/-0.5 s lag search. Median fall rate 0.96 dbar/s. FP07 time constant: SUSPECT: 4-5 ms here against 22-25 ms in 2021 and March 2022, with the pair's 20 Hz ratio reversed. T2's quiet-window floor is 1.5x its noise model at 60-100 Hz and up to 23x at 150-250 Hz (T1 about 1): most likely contamination on the T2 channel, not a faster bead (unverified).
